title: Strategic open model selection & catalog walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE+SE ran a focused walkthrough of the model catalog, benchmark interpretation, and the compatibility matrix. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for PHI-adjacent workloads; key concerns: latency SLA, quantization tradeoffs, and data residency/SOC2. Agreed next steps: run a 48h perf benchmark on Arcadia sample prompts, share security pack and pricing, schedule a Dedicated sizing call.
topics: Interpreting benchmark percentiles and tail latency
Compatibility matrix mapping to GPU types
next_steps: Redwood to run 48h perf benchmark with Arcadia prompt set (Liam)
Send SOC2 + security pack and KMS integration notes (Maya)
Share preliminary Dedicated sizing and pricing options (Maya)
Schedule follow-up: Dedicated sizing deep dive with infra team (w/ Jared)
action_items: Liam O'Connor: Kick off benchmark run with Arcadia prompts and share raw logs (due 2025-12-10)
Maya Patel: Email security artifacts + privacy note and pricing summary (due 2025-12-09)
Jared Kim: Provide sample prompt corpus and 95th percentile latency SLA target (due 2025-12-09)
transcript:
Header: 2025-12-08 15:00 PST | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jared (CTO - Arcadia), Priya (ML Eng), Alma (PM)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya Patel from Redwood, and with me is Liam O'Connor from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Jared: Good, thanks. We've got about an hour. Want to see how you folks are thinking about selecting open models and mapping them to our infra.
[00:12] Maya: Perfect. High level plan — quick catalog tour, a demo of the compatibility matrix, then benchmarking interpretation in Optimize, and we can talk deployment modes for your PHI-adjacent data.
[00:20] Priya: Sounds good. We're especially interested in quantized variants and how you measure accuracy delta.
[00:24] Liam: Cool. I'll share my screen — okay seeing the Console? (brief pause) Looks like the filter pane is on the left.
[00:30] [00:30] Speaker 2: (screen share audio) yeah i can see
[00:33] Liam: Great. So here is our open-model catalog slice — you'll see models grouped by family, plus metadata: tokenization, typical per-token cost, sequence length distribution, and pre-run benchmark scores. Note the benchmark table reports median, p95, and tail latencies — the p95 is your standard SLA proxy.
[00:50] Priya: Are those running on A100s? The compatibility matrix lists a mix of Ampere and Hopper.
[00:55] Liam: Benchmarks tag the hardware — we run on both A100 and H100. The compatibility matrix maps model variants to recommended hardware and quantization profiles. For example, a 4-bit q4 variant for LM-1 maps well to H100 but on Ampere you may see different kernel paths and slightly higher tail.
[01:12] Alma: Real quick — what's the accuracy delta for q4?
[01:15] Liam: It depends by workload. In our Optimize dashboard we show delta on representative eval sets — for a summarization set we saw ~0.8-1.8% ROUGE drop, but for instruction-following prompts it can be sub-1%. We always recommend running a target prompt set.
[01:30] [01:30] Maya: Quick note — we can add an Arcadia-specific eval to Optimize so you get a direct comparo across model + quant combos.
[01:36] Jared: That would be ideal.
[01:37] Priya: For the compatibility matrix, how do you encode sequence length variance? Our calls are mostly 1-2k tokens but occasionally go to 8k.
[01:45] Liam: The matrix includes recommended configs per sequence bucket. For longer sequences we bias toward models with kv-cache optimizations; on the matrix you'll see a 'sequence sweetspot' column. Note that longer sequences amplify tail latency — that's where our routing rules (prefix routing + fallback to a higher-capacity variant) help.
[02:02] [02:02] Jared: Quick question on routing — is automatic fallback only between model variants, or between deployment tiers (hosted -> dedicated)?
[02:09] Maya: Both. Policies can fall back horizontally to a cheaper variant or vertically to a different capacity tier. You can set SLA gates like 95th latency thresholds. If the primary model misses the gate we can route to a higher-throughput instance or a different model with a safety net.
[02:25] Priya: Are there any gotchas with KV cache when you have quantization + batching? I heard sometimes cache keys mismatch?
[02:31] Liam: Good question. In practice we manage the KV cache abstracts inside the runtime; the common issues are around kernel compatibility. Sometimes the quantized path uses a different kernel set which requires different cache layout — occasionally transcription or perf notes in our reports call it "KV cat" or "KV catche" in auto transcripts — but that just means the caching path changed. We surface any such incompatibilities in the compatibility matrix and the per-model notes.
[02:54] Alma: How do you interpret benchmark percentiles — are these single-stream or multi-stream?
[02:58] Liam: Benchmarks in the catalog are mixed: single-stream for latency-sensitive models and multi-worker throughput tests for batching analysis. In Optimize you can view request-distribution histograms — that helps you size Dedicated pools.
[03:12] [03:12] Maya: Let me jump to an example. Here is LM-2 (open) at q4 on H100: median 60ms, p95 180ms. On A100 median 70ms, p95 250ms. That's a decent delta to consider for SLA planning.
[03:27] Priya: And cost difference?
[03:29] Maya: Cost-per-token delta is also shown — on average the H100 run with q4 nets ~14% lower token cost due to kernel efficiency and lower tail resource consumption. We surface all of this in the per-model cost breakdown.
[03:42] Jared: Security — if we move to Private, do you support our KMS and on-prem HSM?
[03:46] Liam: Yes. Private deployments integrate customer KMS (we support a list of KMS vendors) and HSM for key wrapping. We also provide audit logs, SAML SSO, RBAC, and retention controls — full SOC2 artifacts in the security pack.
[03:59] Alma: Any constraints for PHI in hosted? We are leaning Private for regulatory peace of mind.
[04:03] Maya: For PHI-adjacent workloads we typically recommend Private or Dedicated with VPC peering and strict routing. Hosted can be acceptable with a strong DPA and encryption-only approaches, but many healthcare customers prefer dedicated or private.
[04:18] [04:18] Jared: Pricing — what's the sizing model for Dedicated? We need predictable throughput for triage workflows.
[04:23] Maya: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with burst capacity. We produce a sizing recommendation based on your qps, avg tokens, and desired p95. We'll run a 48h benchmark using your prompt set to generate a recommended configuration and cost estimate.
[04:38] Priya: Good. On the benchmark run, can you capture tail distributions and raw logs? We might want to replay some sequences to reproduce anomalies.
[04:44] Liam: Absolutely — we'll share raw perf logs and the Optimize export so you can replay offline.
[04:49] [04:49] Maya: We also wanted to show the Model Playbook note area — here we document tradeoffs, known regressions, and rollout guides for each catalog entry. For example, LM-3 q3 had a recent regression on hallucination with code prompts — we add a "do not serve" flag until patch.
[05:09] Jared: Nice. Who maintains that playbook?
[05:11] Liam: Our model ops team curates it; customers can also submit feedback which becomes part of the playbook entry.
[05:16] Alma: Any other vendor lock concerns? If we pull a model variant and later swap to a different architecture, how disruptive is the API?
[05:23] Maya: Our API abstraction keeps prompts and calls consistent. You can pin a model family version and roll to a different architecture with a config change. The main disruption can be in prompt tuning or eval regressions, which is why we recommend pre-rollout canaries and A/B tests — the Console supports that.
[05:39] [05:39] Priya: One last technical — how are quantization recommendations derived? Based on int8/4-bit accuracy curves?
[05:45] Liam: Yes, we generate accuracy vs perf curves per model on standard evals and your evals. The compatibility matrix shows recommended quant levels by workload type. We also annotate when a quantized kernel path relies on a particular CUDA or runtime version — that's important for Dedicated/on-prem.
[05:59] Jared: Great. Anything else on the catalog side?
[06:02] Maya: Quick recap of immediate next steps — we'll run the 48h perf benchmark, send the security pack + SOC2, and share preliminary Dedicated sizing and pricing.
[06:10] Jared: Sounds good. Can we get the benchmark started by Monday?
[06:13] Liam: We'll start on Monday morning; expecting results within 48h.
[06:17] Maya: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the Dedicated sizing deep dive.
[06:20] Alma: Thanks all.

Notes / Links referenced: Catalog CSV: drive.redwood.com/catalog/arcadia-compat.xlsx (shared), Optimize eval: optimize.redwood.com/arcadia-eval (internal link), Security pack (link to drive).

End of transcript.
